_comment: How each result in this directory was produced. 'mode' is the field that
matters to the checker: a read-only run cannot write a spec file, so its
SP-1 evidence is a NAMED path at best and often NONE. Grading it against a
spec_file_prefix would fail it for a permission decision rather than for a
routing decision, so check_results.py skips that one assertion and says so.
This is the machine-readable form of the evidence file's 'three
envelope: TASK.md, byte-identical across all three fixtures

codex.model: gpt-5.6-terra, effort medium (config default; argv echoed at start)

claude.note: Reported 'Ignoring 4 permissions.allow entries from .claude/settings.json: this workspace has not been trusted' and completed anyway. The fixture's settings file is a decoy, so ignoring it is correct - but this run is therefore not evidence about settings-driven routing.

cursor.invocation: cursor-agent -p --trust --mode ask --model auto "<envelope, amended to print the report to stdout>"
cursor.note: --trust clears the workspace-trust gate but grants no tools; writes need -f/--yolo, which the controller's classifier refuses. Recorded as B13 in herdr-ops/FINDINGS.md. Verified read-only after the fact: every fixture file's mtime predates the run.

agy.invocation: agy --mode plan --dangerously-skip-permissions --model gemini-3.1-pro-high --effort high --print-timeout 20m -p="<envelope, amended to print the report to stdout>"
agy.note: Run by the operator: agy has no per-invocation read-only grant, and --dangerously-skip-permissions is refused to the controller in every mode. The model pin is load-bearing - agy's default is gemini-3.7-flash-high, a flash model, and it follows the head of the catalogue rather than a stored setting.
